rationale: #924 (swift half, M60 name surface — found by the R10 whitespace-class split, script/m60/target-spelling-census.ts). An enum case with a preceding `@available(...)` attribute puts a `modifiers` node FIRST, so the member-name pick (`firstNamedChild`) published the ATTRIBUTE PAYLOAD as the member's name. Measured on swift-nio/Sources/NIOHTTP1/HTTPTypes.swift: five cases (`invalidHost`, `invalidPort`, `invalidPath`, `invalidQueryString`, `invalidFragment`) were absent as symbols, and the artifact carried one `contains HTTPParserError -> @available(*, deprecated, message: "Cannot be thrown")` whose 'name' is a decorator payload. The name is the identifier after `case`; the attribute is metadata. This fixture spells two DIFFERENT payloads, because the corpus's five are IDENTICAL and a revert would otherwise collapse into one target and could hide. The pins: both real names exist with their owner; no symbol and no relationship target carries the payload; the unattributed case and a real construction from a (now-correctly named) attributed case still work.

expectSymbols.name: invalidHost
expectSymbols.note: the name is the identifier after `case`, never the `modifiers` node

expectRelationships.note: M59.A7: the declaration's own line — the `case` line (30), not the `@available` line above it (29)
the named case resolves against the correctly-named member set

forbidSymbols.name: @available(*, deprecated, message: "Cannot be thrown")
forbidSymbols.comment: #924: a decorator PAYLOAD is not a name — pre-fix this was the enum member's published name

forbidSymbols.name: @available(*, deprecated, message: "Legacy spelling")
forbidSymbols.comment: the second spelling, so the revert cannot hide behind the corpus's identical strings

forbidRelationships.comment: #924: the payload must never be a target either
